Internal helper: the column widths of a table, in dxa

Source: R/tables.R
dot-jst_docx_widths.Rd

From the widest text each column holds at the style's size, in the table's font and bold where the style sets it bold (Session 407), plus the cell margins; a column of numbers at least as wide as its block, the widest whole part beside the widest tail (Session 405); the stub from every row's label, a heading row's too, each beside its indent (Session 407); a spanner's label spread over its columns when it is wider than they are.

Usage

.jst_docx_widths(tbl, style, size = NULL, pad = 120L, headings = TRUE)

Arguments

tbl

A jst_table.

style

The style list.

size

Points, or NULL for the style's size.

pad

The twips added to each number column beside its margins (120; a table fitted to the page gives up half of it first, Session 403).

headings

FALSE for the stub from the data rows alone: the width at which no data label wraps, which the page fit and its report read (a heading row spans the table, so in a table fitted to its page the stub may narrow past it, and the heading runs on over the numbers).

Value

Integer vector, one per column.
